334451.title: The fixed-size independent-set extremal conjecture
334451.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph with $2ad$ vertices, and let $i_t(G)$ denote the number of independent sets of size $t$ in $G$. Recall that $aK_{d,d}$ is the disjoint union of $a$ copies of $K_{d,d}$. **Fixed-size independent-set conjecture.** For every $t$,

$$
i_t(G)\le i_t(aK_{d,d}).
$$

This asserts that the disjoint union of complete bipartite graphs, already extremal for the total number of independent sets, is extremal at every fixed size. The conjecture remains open, with partial bounds known.
334451.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: For every d,a,t prove the coefficientwise independent-set comparison, not merely a partition-function inequality at each positive fugacity. Pointwise polynomial domination does not imply coefficientwise domination. No source body read in this pass.

334603.title: Iterated difference-product growth conjecture
334603.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite set, and for a positive integer $k$ write

$$
(A-A)^{(k)}=\underbrace{(A-A)\cdots(A-A)}_{k\text{ factors}}.
$$

Here $X\gg_{k,l}Y$ means that $X\geq c_{k,l}Y$ for a positive constant depending only on $k$ and $l$. **Iterated difference-product growth conjecture.** For every $l>0$ there exists $k>0$ such that, uniformly for all sets $A\subset\mathbb{R}$,

$$
|(A-A)^{(k)}|\gg_{k,l}|A|^l.
$$

This conjecture predicts arbitrarily large polynomial growth from sufficiently many iterated products of a difference set. The paper notes that even the case $l=3$ appears beyond the methods developed there; no resolution is supplied.
334603.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Need for every real l>0 a single integer k and positive constant valid for ALL finite A; one fixed superquadratic exponent cannot be iterated without a growth-stability lemma for the new sets. Primary body unread.

334604.title: Small-product-set difference containment conjecture
334604.statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite real set, and let $XX=\{xy:x,y\in X\}$. Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a set with difference set $A-A=\{a-a':a,a'\in A\}$. **Small-product-set difference containment conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that, for every real set $X$ satisfying

$$
|XX|\leq |X|^{1+\delta},
$$

if

$$
A-A\subset X,
$$

then

$$
|A|\ll_\delta |X|^\epsilon.
$$

This is presented as an alternative form of the iterated difference-product conjecture: a set with very small multiplicative doubling should not contain the difference set of a substantially larger set. The source gives no resolution.
334604.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Need epsilon-to-delta uniformity and a bound with constant depending only on delta, for every finite X and A-A subset X. A small product-set theorem on X alone does not constrain an arbitrary difference subset to the required subpower size. Primary body unread.

334833.title: Conjecture on random Kneser graph chromatic number
334833.statement:
Let $KG_{n,k}$ be the Kneser graph on the $k$-element subsets of $[n]$, and let $KG_{n,k}(p)$ be its random subgraph obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. Write $\chi$ for chromatic number. **Random Kneser graph conjecture.** For every fixed $p>0$,

$$
\chi\bigl(KG_{n,k}(p)\bigr)\ge \chi\bigl(KG_{n,k}\bigr)-4
$$

whenever $k\gg\log n$. This conjecture proposes that, in the indicated range, passing to a random subgraph lowers the chromatic number by at most an additive constant; the supplied passage states that the corresponding question is open and gives no resolution of this conjecture.
334833.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Literal record omits an explicit high-probability qualifier. A random subgraph can lose all edges with positive probability whenever p<1 and the finite parent has edges; deterministic interpretation cannot be the intended asymptotic statement. Need actual source quantifiers and a simultaneous coloring obstruction in k>>log n. No endpoint correction credit; primary body unread.

336680.title: Cyclic groups minimize the number of connected components of power maps
336680.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group of order $n$, let $C_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$, and let $N(a,G)$ be the number of connected components of the functional graph $G(a,G)$ associated with the power map $x\mapsto x^a$. **Cyclic-group minimization conjecture.** For every $a$, one has

$$
N(a,G)\geq N(a,C_n).
$$

The conjecture asserts that cyclic groups have the fewest connected components among groups of a given order. The source gives no further evidence for its resolution.

341889.title: Guy's conjecture on eventual periodicity of finite octal-game Grundy sequences
341889.statement:
An **octal game** is a taking-and-breaking game in which a move never splits a pile into more than two piles; a finite octal game is specified by finitely many allowed moves. Its Grundy sequence is the integer sequence whose $i$-th term is the Grundy value of the position consisting of one pile of $i$ tokens.

**Guy's conjecture.** Every finite octal game has an eventually periodic Grundy sequence.

This is a famous conjecture in combinatorial game theory; the supplied text does not state a resolution.

342468.title: Meunier's chromatic number conjecture for stable Kneser graphs
342468.statement:
Let $KG(n,k)_{s-\mathrm{stab}}$ be the induced subgraph of the Kneser graph $KG(n,k)$ on the $s$-stable $k$-subsets of $[n]$, where a subset $A$ is $s$-stable when $s\leq |i-j|\leq n-s$ for every pair of distinct elements $i,j\in A$. **Meunier's conjecture.** If $n,k,s$ are non-negative integers such that $n\geq sk$ and $s\geq 2$, then

$$
\chi\left(KG(n,k)_{s-\mathrm{stab}}\right)=n-s(k-1).
$$

This generalizes the chromatic-number formula for Schrijver graphs, which are the case $s=2$. The source presents the assertion as Meunier's conjecture; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
342468.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Source p.2 Conjecture1 matches displayed formula and reports even-s and large-n partial cases; conclusion notes neighborhood connectivity cannot in general deliver the desired s=3 bound. 346284.title: Aharoni–Howard conjecture on rainbow matchings
346284.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, write $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ be the family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$. Let $\mathcal F=\{F_1,\ldots,F_t\}$ be a family of subsets of $\binom{[n]}{k}$, and call a set of pairwise disjoint edges, one from each $F_i$, a **rainbow matching**. **Aharoni–Howard conjecture.** If

$$
e(F_i)>\max\left\{\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-t+1}{k},\binom{kt-1}{k}\right\}
$$

for every $1\le i\le t$, then $\mathcal F$ admits a rainbow matching. This is the family version of the Erdős matching conjecture and seeks a sharp edge-density condition guaranteeing a rainbow matching; the source provides no evidence of resolution.
346284.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Need one simultaneous matching choosing disjoint representatives from ALL t families under the maximum of the two stated thresholds. Ordinary matching in each family separately does not provide rainbow compatibility. No full primary-body review.

375887.title: Frankl's binomial norm conjecture for intersecting-union families
375887.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ denote its power set, and let an **IU-family** be a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ in which any two members intersect and no two members cover $[n]$. Define its **binomial norm** by

$$
\lVert\mathcal F\rVert_n=\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\binom{n}{|F|}^{-1}.
$$

**Frankl's conjecture.** For every IU-family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$,

$$
\lVert\mathcal F\rVert_n\leq \frac{n+1}{6}.
$$

Frankl's circle-method argument gives the weaker bound $\lVert\mathcal F\rVert_n\leq n/4$; the conjectured sharp constant remains unresolved.
375887.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Need all-level reciprocal-binomial bound (n+1)/6 for every intersecting and co-noncovering family. Separate intersection bounds or n/4 circle bound do not yield the sharper coupled constraint. Actual 2026 primary and four listed companion bodies unread; current status not cleared.

329849.title: Large-uniformity conjecture for hypergraphs without regular subgraphs
329849.statement:
For a positive integer $r$, let $k_r$ and $n_k$ be thresholds, and let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph. A **full $k$-star** is the family of all $k$-edges containing a fixed vertex. **Large-uniformity regular-subgraph conjecture.** For every $r$, there exist $k_r$ and $n_k$ such that, whenever $k>k_r$, $n>n_k$, and $r\mid k$, every $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with no $r$-regular subgraphs satisfies

$$
|H|\leq {{n-1}\choose{k-1}},
$$

and equality holds if and only if $H$ is a full $k$-star. This proposes the full star as the extremal example beyond the range proved in the main theorem; the source gives no resolution status.

329972.title: The Galton–Watson conjecture for degree-weighted CMP

for every $c>0$. **Galton–Watson degree-weighted CMP conjecture.** Degree-weighted CMP on $G$ with expansion exponent $\alpha$ has a non-trivial phase transition, meaning that its critical parameter satisfies $0<p_c<1$. This is presented as an expected extension for degree-weighted CMP; the conjecture is left open in the paper.

329993.title: Residue-class unimodality conjecture for rational Catalan polynomials
329993.statement:
Let $a<b$ be relatively prime, and write

$$
\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)=\sum_j c_jq^j.
$$

For each residue class $r$ with $0\leq r<a$, consider the coefficient sequence $(c_{ak+r})_k$ indexed by the integers $k$ for which these coefficients occur.

**Residue-class unimodality conjecture.** For every residue class $r$, $0\leq r<a$, the coefficients of $q^{ak+r}$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)$ are unimodal. The conjecture refines ordinary unimodality, which the source notes does not hold for the coefficients of $\mathbf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)$ in general. It is motivated by the shifted-coset formula above, but no resolution is supplied.
329993.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Need each fixed residue coefficient sequence of the literal rational Catalan polynomial, uniformly in coprime a<b. 330385.title: The prime-torsion conjecture for poset Lie algebra homology
330385.statement: Let $\preceq$ be the poset defining the poset Lie algebra $\frak{gl}_n^\preceq$, and let $H_\ast(\frak{gl}_n^\preceq;\mathbb{Z})$ denote its homology with integer coefficients. For a prime $p$, say that the homology contains $p$-torsion if some homology group has an element of order divisible by $p$. **Prime-torsion conjecture.** If $H_\ast(\frak{gl}_n^\preceq;\mathbb{Z})$ contains $p$-torsion, then it contains $p'$-torsion for every prime $p'<p$. This predicts that torsion primes in the homology occur without gaps below any torsion prime. The surrounding result shows that absence of $2$-torsion forces the Hasse diagram to be a forest of height at most $1$ and the homology to be torsion-free; the stated implication for all primes is not established here.
330385.remaining_exact_lemma_or_gate: Need an integral homology transfer detecting every smaller prime whenever p-torsion occurs, for the entire defining poset. Rational homology or the special no-2-torsion theorem cannot establish propagation among all odd primes. Primary body unread.

330479.title: Shareshian–Wachs generalized q-Eulerian q-unimodality conjecture
330479.statement:
For $\sigma\in{\mathfrak S}_n$, define

$$
{\rm inv}_{<r}(\sigma)=\left|\{(i,j):i<j,\ 0<\sigma(i)-\sigma(j)<r\}\right|,
$$

and

$$
{\rm maj}_{\geq r}(\sigma)=\sum_{i:\,\sigma(i)-\sigma(i+1)\geq r}i.
$$

For $r\in[n]$, set

$$
A_n^{(r)}(q,t)=\sum_{\sigma\in{\mathfrak S}_n}q^{{\rm maj}_{\geq r}(\sigma)}t^{{\rm inv}_{<r}(\sigma)}.
$$

**Shareshian and Wachs's conjecture.** For all $r\in[n]$, the palindromic polynomial $A_n^{(r)}(q,t)$ is $q$-unimodal. This is presented as a consequence of the chromatic-quasisymmetric-function conjecture. The source records the related unimodality question for $A_n^{(r)}(1,t)$ as still open.
